slides.headline: THE PERSON MAYO CLINIC HIRED TO KEEP THEIR AI SAFE IS NOW SUING THEM FOR HIDING ITS 67% ERROR RATE ON REAL PATIENTS
THE AI FAILED TWO OUT OF THREE PATIENTS
slides.body: This wasn't a test run. The tool was live on real patients at one of the most trusted hospitals on earth. The numbers were bad enough to end careers

slides.headline: MAYO BURIED THE NUMBERS AND LEFT THE AI RUNNING
slides.body: Instead of pulling the AI, Mayo concealed the failure rate and left it running on patients. The person who caught it was pushed aside. What they buried is worse than anyone thinks

slides.headline: A COIN FLIP WOULD HAVE BEEN MORE ACCURATE
slides.body: A coin flip gets it right 50% of the time. This AI got it right 33%. Someone at Mayo was hired specifically to make sure this never happened

slides.headline: MAYO HIRED THEM TO PREVENT EXACTLY THIS
slides.body: Mayo hired one person to guard against bad AI. That person checked the tool, found it broken, and raised the alarm. The hospital buried it. Now the guard is the one suing

slides.headline: MAYO HAD ONE PERSON CHECKING. MOST BUSINESSES HAVE ZERO
slides.body: If your business uses AI on customers and nobody's checking accuracy, you have Mayo's blind spot. They found out from a lawsuit. You could find out from one audit

slides.headline: FOLLOW NOW BEFORE THE ALGORITHM HIDES THIS PAGE FROM YOU
slides.body: Send this to the friend who works in healthcare and hasn't asked how accurate their AI is

caption:
Swipe to see how Mayo Clinic's AI failed patients worse than a coin flip, and who's suing them for hiding it 🔬

Mayo Clinic ran an AI tool on real patients that was wrong 67% of the time, their own safety lead found the failure rate, the hospital buried the results and kept the tool running, the AI performed worse than a coin flip, the person hired to prevent AI risk is now the plaintiff suing the hospital, and most businesses using AI today have no one checking if it works.

AI is spreading through hospitals and businesses faster than anyone can audit it. Mayo had a safety lead and still buried a 67% failure rate. Most companies have no one checking at all.
